phase.summary: Phase 1 (Opus architecture) is complete and settled. Phase 2 is implementing the seven components against it. T-01, T-02, T-07, T-09, T-03, T-13 and T-10 resolved earlier; this banking adds T-11, which CLOSES THE ROTATION LOOP and turns the canonical location into an enforced control. A cleared session now reorients itself automatically from banked state (pointer brief, hard 10,000-char cap), verifies its actual cwd, repository root, branch and HEAD against that state before any implementation, and is refused Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and mutating Bash by a committed PreToolUse gate whenever it is in the wrong place - absolute-path luck is explicitly not a control. Both hooks are activated by a committed idempotent installer, which also reconciled the long-dangling ensure-watcher SessionStart hook. T-14 (build-session registry/launcher by name, automatic programme PR, exact-head QA binding, single merge decision) is now THE next action; T-04 (evaluator) remains independently takable.

tickets.title: Pure evaluator: evaluate(signals) to verdict
tickets.note: 34/34 ticket tests, including a full 64-combination power-set sweep over the 6-signal vocabulary (contextUsedPercentage, rateLimitFiveHourUsedPercentage, growthProjectedRedBeforeCompletion, compactions, bankedStateStale, safeBoundary) asserting the verdict shape stays valid and BLIND fires iff contextUsedPercentage is absent, for every combination. 420/420 suite-wide, no regressions. AD-11 purity: zero filesystem/git/myPKA imports (evaluate(signals) takes a plain object only). Priority BLIND > RECOVERY > RED > AMBER > GREEN, five distinct exit codes (0-4). Missing-field semantics: only contextUsedPercentage is required; every other absent signal is unknown, skipped, and never escalates to BLIND on its own. Judgement call recorded: section 4's states table defines RECOVERY as authoritative-state-already-lost and places it OFF the main axis, while the adjacent threshold bullets describe compaction count as an AMBER/RED FLOOR on that axis -- the two do not fully agree. This implementation takes the states table as authoritative: any compaction (>=1) this session, or a banked state known stale vs live git HEAD, resolves to RECOVERY outright (outranking RED), not merely a floor -- because INV-3 says degraded in-context memory is not something a low context percentage should be able to mask. safeBoundary modulates advice text only ('rotate now' vs 'reach a safe boundary urgently' vs unknown), never the state itself, per section 4's explicit instruction.

tickets.title: Windows-safe atomic write: retry the rename, and never orphan a temp file
tickets.note: Built by Keel under WO-2026-08-01-01, AMENDED after Keel returned CLARIFY and caught that Larry's own load-bearing criterion (AC4, 'assert a non-zero success count') was SATISFIABLE BY THE UNFIXED CODE - measured 47 of 48 writers succeeding against the broken writeHealthSample, so the test would have gone green on the defect it existed to catch. AC4 was rewritten to successCount === N with reader contention and a made-to-fail control. Keel also corrected the mechanism: EPERM is driven by a concurrent READER holding the target across the rename, not writer-vs-writer, which is why delegation-gate (reads every call) was flakier than health-store (never reads). One shared primitive tools/governor/atomic-write.mjs with exported policy (RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES, MAX_ATTEMPTS 5, RETRY_BUDGET_MS 250, BACKOFF_MS 10/20/40/80, BACKOFF_JITTER 0.5 - jitter added for a MEASURED reason, an unjittered lockstep retry was a thundering herd of the module's own making). delegation-gate passes a payload PRODUCER re-invoked per attempt (M1: replaying a stale snapshot would let a later rename discard another writer's records, converting lose-one into lose-several); health-store passes a constant. 19 new tests, 607/607 suite-wide. Both protected test files BYTE-UNMODIFIED and absent from the commit. delegation-gate.test.mjs 8/8 consecutive runs (was 9 pass / 3 fail over 12); health-store.test.mjs 6/6 (was 5/6). Secret scan exit 0 over the declared surface. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY LARRY with his own reader-contended probe against the real module, and the result is MIXED and recorded as such: ORPHANED TEMP FILES ARE FIXED - 0 orphans against a 7-orphan baseline on the same shape - but under CONTINUOUS reader hammering (16 readers in a tight loop for 2.5s, harsher than Keel's 25-read burst) 13 of 16 writer processes STILL FAIL. KEEL DISCLOSED THIS LIMIT PLAINLY rather than letting the green imply otherwise ('writers still fail 2-6 of 16 even with the retry; no policy inside the ceiling can fix that'), and Larry's probe confirms it is real and is worse at higher intensity. The 250ms ceiling was LARRY'S constraint (M2/M3, set because a PreToolUse hook that blocks longer is a gate in the way, AD-19) and Keel correctly refused to raise it unilaterally. SO WHAT T-18 ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the orphan leak is closed outright; the retry substantially reduces but does NOT eliminate writer failure under sustained reader contention. Both callers still fail SAFE on a lost write (health sample -> BLIND/stale per AD-3; delegation checkpoint -> undercount toward a missed deny). DEFERRED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, per Warwick's scope freeze 2026-08-01: (a) the residual high-contention failure band, which needs either a wider budget than a hook can afford or a different mechanism than retry; (b) T-19/D-6, the three remaining unretried sites (build-registry.mjs:275, programme-state.mjs:630 and :638, qa-binding.mjs:288) and the false 'never interleave' comment that propagated by citation; (c) Keel's reported contradiction between AC4 clause 5 (orphans non-zero on the failure variant) and AC3 (zero orphans on every path) - clause 5 was written against pre-fix behaviour that AC3 abolishes; Keel satisfied the intent with two variants and did NOT amend the criterion itself. POSIX behaviour unproven - this is a Windows phenomenon.

blockers.summary: The estate's atomic-write primitive is not concurrency-safe on Windows, and T-02's evidence overstates what it proved. health-store.mjs (T-02) and delegation-gate.mjs (T-16) both write a unique temp file then renameSync onto the target with NO retry. On Windows that rename throws EPERM when another process holds the target. MEASURED by Larry on 2026-08-01, not inferred: health-store failed 21 of 48 writer processes under 16 concurrent processes (44%); delegation-gate's own CONCURRENCY test (N concurrent appender processes never produce a torn or corrupt ledger file) fails roughly 2 runs in 5 when run in isolation - the builder reported it as a one-off flake, but it reproduces. T-02's note cites a 12-process concurrent-write mutation test as proof; what that test actually established is that the file is never TORN (true - rename is all-or-nothing), NOT that concurrent writers succeed. They frequently do not. This is the state-what-was-PROVEN-not-what-it-implies failure mode, and the full-suite green (588/588) hides it because the failure is probabilistic and the suite happened to pass. SECONDARY: a failed rename orphans its temp file permanently - 21 accumulated in the real health store during the probe and had to be removed by hand.
blockers.recommendation: Fix in T-18: bounded retry with backoff on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES around the rename, temp-file cleanup in a finally so a failure never orphans, applied to the ONE shared primitive rather than copy-pasted into two modules. The concurrency proof must assert a non-zero SUCCESS count, not merely the absence of tearing - a test that passes when every writer fails is the exact vacuous-green shape AD-24 already refuses elsewhere. DIRECTION OF HARM IS SAFE BUT NOT NIL, and this is why it is a defect rather than a curiosity: a lost health sample degrades to BLIND/stale (AD-3, safe) and a lost delegation checkpoint undercounts toward a MISSED deny (discipline gate, bounded) - but T-03's sampler is intended to run on EVERY assistant message from the live statusLine, which is precisely the high-concurrency path this primitive fails on, so the real-world hit rate rises sharply the moment that wiring is activated.

blockers.summary: A false concurrency-safety claim has propagated across three modules BY CITATION. qa-binding.mjs:282-284 states: 'A write killed mid-flight leaves the previous good file untouched; two concurrent writers never interleave. Same recipe as health-store.mjs and writeProgrammeState.' The non-interleaving half is true and the durability half is true, but together they read as a concurrency-safety guarantee the code does not provide - concurrent writers do not interleave, they FAIL with EPERM (see D-5, measured). health-store.mjs's header carries the same overclaim, and qa-binding.mjs explicitly cites it and writeProgrammeState as precedent, which is how one module's overstated comment became three modules' shared belief. This is a documentation defect with real consequence: it is the reason the pattern was copied forward unexamined into build-registry.mjs, programme-state.mjs and qa-binding.mjs.
blockers.recommendation: Correct the comments in T-19 alongside adopting the shared primitive. State what is actually true: the write is atomic (never torn, never partially visible) and durable against a mid-flight kill, and separately state whether concurrent writers SUCCEED - which after T-18 they do, by bounded retry, and before T-18 they frequently did not. Do not simply delete the comments; an absent claim invites the next author to re-derive the same wrong one. This is the estate's 'state what was PROVEN, not what it implies' rule applied to a code comment.

locked_decisions.decision: statusLine is the primary telemetry source; the transcript is corroboration only, and must always be tail-read.
locked_decisions.why: statusLine is a documented, stable contract; the transcript format is explicitly internal and version-fragile, and several local transcripts are 30-40 MB.

locked_decisions.decision: Two separate stores: session health (ephemeral, machine-local) and programme state (durable, git-versioned).
locked_decisions.why: Different lifetimes and audiences. Conflating them is how banked state gets lost.

locked_decisions.decision: BLIND is a first-class state with its own exit code. Unreadable telemetry is never GREEN.
locked_decisions.why: INV-1, and the direct lesson of the 2026-07-29 controls that reported success over ground they never examined.

locked_decisions.decision: Compaction is counted by the PreCompact hook, never inferred from the transcript.
locked_decisions.why: A local probe found zero reliable transcript markers for compaction.

locked_decisions.decision: Reorientation rides SessionStart(source="clear") to additionalContext, capped at 10,000 characters, so the injected brief is a POINTER document and not the state itself.
locked_decisions.why: The cap makes a full state dump impossible.

locked_decisions.decision: The RED preflight block fails OPEN.
locked_decisions.why: INV-2. A governor that traps Warwick in his own session is a worse defect than one that misses a rotation.

locked_decisions.decision: The map lives in git as markdown, not in an issue tracker.
locked_decisions.why: Subagents get no MCP tools, so a tracker-hosted map is unreadable by the very workers who need it.

locked_decisions.decision: The evaluator core is pure: evaluate(signals) to verdict, with zero filesystem, git or myPKA knowledge. Adapters gather signals.
locked_decisions.why: Portability, and it makes the state space unit-testable without an estate.

locked_decisions.decision: The Governor DERIVES Team Knowledge/fusion-brief/session-handoff.md; it never invents a rival handoff file.
locked_decisions.why: That file already declares itself as consumed by the next Larry session. A parallel handoff would create two competing SSOTs — the exact defect this build exists to prevent.

locked_decisions.decision: /rotate-session inherits close-session steps 1-3 only. Steps 4-7 (Librarian pass, graduation, ClickUp mirror, self-improvement review) are end-of-programme and must never run on a rotation.
locked_decisions.why: INV-4. A rotation that costs what a close costs will not get used, and an unused governor is worse than none.

locked_decisions.decision: Durable programme state lives at <programme.home>/programme-state.json — with the programme, on the programme’s branch — and banked.head_sha records the head the state DESCRIBES, i.e. the parent of the commit that carries the state file.
locked_decisions.why: A file cannot contain its own commit’s SHA. State banked on a feature branch describes commits that exist only on that branch, so parking it on main would make it lie the moment the branch advanced. Consumers comparing against live HEAD must exclude the banking commit itself.

locked_decisions.decision: The programme-state collector (T-13) never performs a git fetch, so branches.behind is permanently unknown under it.
locked_decisions.why: A trustworthy behind-count needs fresh remote-tracking refs, and a collector must not have side effects on the repository it is reporting on. Matches this document's own pre-existing branches.behind unknown declaration from T-09.

locked_decisions.decision: T-13 collects repository, worktrees, branches and pull_requests only. workers is never scanned or synthesised by the collector.
locked_decisions.why: Which subagent was dispatched, for which ticket, with what expected output, is programme knowledge the dispatching session holds — not something git, worktree-recon or gh can answer. F-7 already establishes live-worker detection is best-effort; inventing worker entries from an OS process scan would manufacture false precision under a field whose entire schema purpose (T-09's D-2) is refusing to let a guessed collection read as ground truth.

locked_decisions.decision: THE ARTEFACT HIERARCHY (settled 2026-07-31, CORRECTED 2026-08-01 after the T-14 dual-write incident, binding). (1) The Goal / Build Contract (01-GOAL-CONTRACT.md) is the PRODUCT SSOT — outcome, invariants, scope. (2) programme-state.json's tickets[] is the EXECUTION-STATE SSOT — which tickets are resolved, what the frontier is, and what resumption points to are facts of THIS document alone; resolveTicket / deriveResumption / resolveTicketAndAdvance / applyTicketResolution in tools/governor/programme-state.mjs are the only sanctioned way to change them. (3) The Wayfinder map (02-MAP.md) is the HUMAN-READABLE NAVIGATION / DECISION PROJECTION — architecture, settled decisions, fog, the ticket-index narrative and the write-back log stay hand-authored, but it NO LONGER ASSERTS TICKET STATUS on its own authority: the GOVERNOR:STATUS block in §8 is machine-rendered from the ledger, and /rotate-session refuses with STALE_EXECUTION_STATE if the two ever disagree. (4) The Implementation Plan is the INITIAL ROUTE ONLY — context, never prescription; superseded by the map the moment execution diverges. (5) programme-state.json as a whole and Team Knowledge/fusion-brief/session-handoff.md are GENERATED PROJECTIONS of the execution-state SSOT — never hand-authored, never a rival source; a disagreement between a projection and its source is a defect in the projection. (6) Before merge, enduring BUILD-018 records GRADUATE into Builds/BUILD-018-session-governor/; evidence may remain under Deliverables/.
locked_decisions.why: Resolves the "which file wins" question that a rotation makes acute: a fresh Larry reads several artefacts and must know their rank without asking. ORIGINALLY THIS AD NAMED THE MAP ITSELF AS AN "EXECUTION SSOT" — the exact ambiguity that caused the incident: T-14 was declared resolved in the map narrative while tickets[] still called it frontier, and the next /rotate-session banked a resumption pointer telling the fresh session to redo finished work. Splitting execution-state SSOT (2) from navigation projection (3) removes the ambiguity structurally: one place ticket status lives, one function allowed to change it, one automated check that refuses to bank a disagreement. Refines AD-9 (map-over-tickets, which is about ticket SPECS not ticket STATUS, and is unaffected) and generalises AD-12 (the handoff is derived, never invented).

locked_decisions.decision: The wrong-worktree gate keys on cwd, repository root and branch ONLY. HEAD is compared and REPORTED, but never denies.
locked_decisions.why: The moment a session makes its first legitimate commit, its HEAD diverges from banked.head_sha. A gate keyed on HEAD would block the session for having succeeded, and would be switched off within the hour. Location is a precondition; head movement is normal progress, and staleness already has its own channel (AD-14).

locked_decisions.decision: Two unknowns, two directions. (a) Cannot establish where we are while a canonical location IS known -> DENY (unknown is never aligned). (b) No active programme found at all, or the guard itself throws -> ALLOW.
locked_decisions.why: Failing closed everywhere would let one guard bug become a total work stoppage on a machine running 22 worktrees; failing open everywhere would make the gate decorative. The split puts the strictness exactly where a canonical location exists to be violated. Threat model is first-party mistakes, not a malicious operator. Both directions are proven by test - an untested fail-direction is an assumption, not a control.

locked_decisions.decision: Warwick never manages branches, worktrees, commits, pushes or PR creation. Larry owns the complete Git lifecycle. Warwick's standing gate is merge-to-main, plus decisions that are genuinely his.
locked_decisions.why: Recorded as a decision rather than left as a habit because the failure it prevents is silent: a Larry that asks Warwick to "just run git checkout" has converted an orchestration failure into Warwick's problem, and the ask looks helpful in the moment. Printed in every reorientation brief and every refusal, so a fresh session inherits it without being told.

locked_decisions.decision: The EnterWorktree recovery protocol. Larry initiates it. Under Remote Control the approval may appear ONLY in the local terminal, so Larry must IMMEDIATELY say, verbatim: "Approve the pending EnterWorktree request in the local Claude terminal", then wait. Larry must NOT spin silently, must NOT continue via absolute paths, and must NOT ask Warwick to run git commands.
locked_decisions.why: Learned live on 2026-07-31: a pending approval invisible to the remote side reads as the assistant hanging, and five minutes vanished. The protocol is embedded verbatim in the deny message and in the brief rather than only in the map, because at the moment it is needed nobody is reading the map - the refusal is the only thing on screen.

locked_decisions.decision: THE ESCALATION RULE (settled 2026-07-31 by Warwick, binding). When a harmless no-action option preserves correctness and avoids additional risk, Larry takes it AUTOMATICALLY and does not ask. Larry must NOT escalate: typos, wording, formatting, naming, cosmetic metadata, ticket boundaries, completed workers, ordinary routing choices, or anything else Larry can safely resolve — and must never offer Warwick a force-push or history-rewrite choice merely to improve cosmetic metadata. Larry escalates ONLY for: a genuine product decision, a material scope change, an unavoidable permission, spend, an irreversible live action, an unsafe repository state, or the final merge decision. This governs AskUserQuestion exactly as it governs ordinary stopping.
locked_decisions.why: An unnecessary escalation is not a neutral courtesy — it is an acceptance failure that costs Warwick's scarce attention and stalls autonomous execution, which is the whole outcome BUILD-018 exists to protect. Warwick's own reasoning for making it mechanical rather than advisory: a Stop hook alone is insufficient, because Larry can manufacture a pause by asking an unnecessary question — so the control must bind the ASK surface, not just the stop surface. Recorded as a decision rather than left as judgement because the failure is silent and looks virtuous in the moment: an unnecessary question reads as diligence, which is exactly why it recurs. The live instance (D-4) had Larry offering to rewrite correct, already-pushed history to fix a stray character in a commit subject.
